about: Extra plain-language explanations for the Error Doctor. Each rule matches part of an error message (not case sensitive) and explains it. {file} and {line} are filled in when the error came from a script. Add your own: that's the 'Teach the Error Doctor' contributor quest.

rules.match: Functions called each other too many times
rules.title: A function that never stops calling itself
rules.explanation: A function calls itself (or two functions call each other) over and over without end. Make sure there's a way out, like an if that stops calling once the job is done.

rules.title: Looping over a number
rules.explanation: 'for' walks through a list of things. To repeat something a number of times, use range: for i in range(10):

rules.title: 'this' is called 'self' here
rules.explanation: Other languages say 'this' for the object the script is on. EasyScript says 'self', like Python. Replace 'this' with 'self' ({file} line {line}).

rules.match: Vectors and colors can't be changed piece by piece
rules.title: Changing part of a vector
rules.explanation: A position or color is one value. To change part of it, make a new one: self.position = vec(5, self.y) instead of changing only its x.

rules.match: Text can't be changed letter by letter
rules.title: Changing one letter of text
rules.explanation: Text can't be edited in place. Build a new piece of text instead, for example: name = name + "!"

rules.title: Using an object after it was destroyed
rules.explanation: The script used an object that no longer exists. After destroy(), don't touch it again. Checking 'if thing:' before using it helps.

rules.match: The dictionary doesn't have the key
rules.title: A missing key in a dictionary
rules.explanation: The dictionary has no entry with that name. Check the spelling, or use 'if key in my_dict:' first.

rules.title: Adding text and a number
rules.explanation: To join text and a number, turn the number into text first: "Score: " + str(score). Or use an f-string: f"Score: {score}"

rules.match: Only sprites and UI elements have a size
rules.title: Size on an object without a picture
rules.explanation: size belongs to sprites and UI. For 3D objects and others, change scale instead: self.scale = vec(2, 2, 2)

rules.title: A sound that won't play
rules.explanation: The sound file is missing or in a format Aven can't read. Aven plays .wav, .mp3, .ogg and .flac files from your project folder.

rules.title: A 3D model that won't load
rules.explanation: Aven loads .gltf and .glb models. Check that the file is in your project, and try exporting it again from your 3D program as glTF 2.0.

rules.title: A line that ends too early
rules.explanation: Something is missing at the end of line {line}: often a closing ) or ], a value after =, or the : at the end of an if or def.

rules.title: A native behavior that isn't built
rules.explanation: An object's NativeScript names a C/C++ behavior that isn't loaded. Open Tools > Native Code and press Build. If it still doesn't appear, check the name you gave aven_behavior() in native/src matches the Inspector exactly (capital letters count).

rules.title: A native library without AVEN_MODULE
rules.explanation: Aven found a library in native/bin but couldn't see what's inside. Each file in native/src becomes its own library, so each one needs AVEN_MODULE(setup) at the end, where setup is the function that calls aven_behavior().

rules.title: A property outside its behavior's data
rules.explanation: aven_number()/aven_integer()/aven_flag() place a property inside your behavior's struct. Pass sizeof(YourStruct) to aven_behavior() and offsetof(YourStruct, field) for each property, so Aven knows where it goes.

rules.title: No CMake to build native code
rules.explanation: Building C/C++ needs CMake and a compiler. Windows: install Visual Studio Community with 'Desktop development with C++' and CMake. macOS: run xcode-select --install and brew install cmake. Linux: install gcc (or clang) and cmake. Then restart Aven so it can find them.
